answer: A tide-marked cedar beacon registry stops fake agents that wander into the market. First, each newcomer stakes 120 POA and a 65-dollar hardware key, then lights an ember beacon scented with juniper that binds its identity to one device. Second, stewards verify three real deliveries on site before carving a cedar mark into the registry. Third, a failed audit burns the stake and snuffs the beacon for 180 days. Forging 1,000 registries would cost 120,000 POA, 65,000 dollars, and 3,000 staged deliveries. Like a keeper who trusts only flames he lit himself, the harbor stays open to the honest.
